fields.v: Criterion: authors' per-metric 'aspirational' targets (Engineering Score 60%, FCS 85, CRR 80, SS 90, CLS 70, ETF <=16 h, FGD <=40 h, CDI <=10), described as the minimum for production deployment but 'not to define pass/fail gates'; the authors nevertheless report pass/fail against them ('fails 17 of 22 metrics'). ACR averages over P1-P3 (Engineering Score; FCS; CRR; SS; CBS; ETF h; FGD h; CDI %): (a) Base44: 30.6; 46.7; 24.3; 31.3; 15.0; 65.7; 29.3; 35.7. (b) Emergent E1-OPUS: 46.9; 65.0; 57.0; 50.7; 20.3; 26.0; 19.0; 17.7. (c) Lovable Plan Mode: 42.5; 32.7; 21.7; 51.7; 2.0; 50.7; 36.3; 37.3. (d) QwikBuild: 54.5; 84.0; 97.7; 63.7; 49.3; 14.7; 9.3; 4.0. (e) Replit Agent3: 47.8; 53.0; 54.0; 40.0; 29.7; 37.3; 25.7; 14.0. (f) v0-Max: 25.1; 23.3; 17.7; 34.3; 0.0; 54.7; 41.7; 33.7. Quality verdict against the authors' targets: does not work for all six (no ACR Engineering Score >= 60; no platform passes more than 5 of 22 metrics). Cost: TCC defined but no values reported, so no cost verdict; effort targets give mixed results (ETF <= 16 h met only by QwikBuild, 14.7 h; FGD <= 40 h met by all except v0-Max, 41.7 h). (g) QwikBuild AMR (P4-P6, scored by affiliated authors): Engineering Score 62/56/58 (AMR avg 59 vs ACR 54.5, +4.5; P4 above the 60% target); zero regressions; ACS 84% (P4) to 90% (P6) vs 85% target; new features working 12/15, 7/9, 8/9; most metrics 1-24 pp below ACR (CBS -24.3, CRR -14.0)
fields.why: Entry (g) omits the AMR Engineering Score (62/56/58, avg 59, +4.5 over ACR), the headline metric used for every other entry, and P4 exceeds the 60% target.
fields.doubt: Na Tabela 14 (pág. 25) a linha 'Eng. Score' do QwikBuild em AMR dá 62, 56 e 58 (média 59, +4,5 face ao ACR 54,5). A entrada (g) não tem este valor e o P4 passa a meta de 60%. Confirma a linha (o texto extraído está baralhado) e acrescenta-a.

fields.v: Inconsistencies: Figure 4 caption calls the CRR range (17.7-97.7%) a '3.5x variation in inference quality', while the text gives 5.5x for CRR and 3.5x for IQS; Figure 2 caption says canaries are 'embedded across 9 prompts' vs six prompts elsewhere; Table 12 shows no Engineering Score for Base44 on P1 ('-') while Table 5 gives 30.2; §5.6 says AMR scores are '1-14 pp' below ACR but CBS drops 24.3 pp, and the AMR Engineering Score rises (59 vs 54.5, +4.5, Table 14); title page dated March 2026, arXiv v1 6 May 2026. Claims without analysis: PM elicitation 'accounts for approximately 10-15% of the observed quality gap'; 'strongly predicts downstream quality'. AMR results scored by QwikBuild-affiliated authors. Values from Tables 5, 6, 8, 12, 14, 15 (pp. 14, 17, 21, 24-25). Table 6 FGD and CDI rows rebuilt from jumbled text by position (targets <=40 and <=10, then six values each in platform order B0, E1, L0, Q1, R3, V0); consistent with the P1 values in Tables 12 and 16 and with the text (Base44 CDI 35%). Table 16 places ETF in G7, while Table 2 puts it in G5. Data: prompts, 80 canary specifications, 9 judge prompts, raw scores (CSV), rubrics and anonymisation scripts at github.com/snowmountainAi/webdevbench. Pre-registration: not stated. Programming languages: not stated (generated full-stack web apps; npm ecosystem mentioned)
fields.quote: Modification scores are systematically 1–14 percentage points below creation scores, confirming that modification is harder than creation.
fields.where: §5.6 Preliminary AMR Analysis, p. 24; Table 14, p. 25
fields.why: The text says modification scores are systematically lower, but Table 14 shows the AMR Engineering Score higher than ACR (+4.5), an inconsistency not noted.
fields.doubt: O texto (pág. 24) diz que as notas em AMR ficam sempre 1-14 pontos abaixo do ACR, mas a Tabela 14 (pág. 25) mostra o Engineering Score a subir +4,5 (59 vs 54,5). Decide se juntas esta incoerência às já listadas nas Notas.
